messages:
sophie: Heads-up — seeing steady memory growth in long-session runs (1k+ token convos) when using INT8 KV profiles. Looks like paging churn + kernel fallback events coincide with small drops in next-token accuracy :thinking_face:
kevin: Can you paste the quick flame/telemetry you have? model, quant profile, and a short repro command would help :eyes:
sophie: repro: `rwd-cli run-profile --model redwood-1-large --quant int8 --session 1400 --batch 1 --workload conv-stress`
sophie: quick perf snippets from the host (trimmed):
```
kv_pages_evicted=1847
kv_pages_loaded=5620
kv_eviction_cycles=23
kernel_select_failures=0.12
kernel_fallback_to_bf16=0.08
mean_mem_per_slot:int8=0.42MB
mean_mem_per_slot:bf16=1.68MB
```
kevin: Interesting — kernel_fallback_to_bf16 at 8% is not negligible. Do you have a per-kernel failure breakdown? That could point to a matmul/contraction path failing on certain sequence lengths.
sophie: yes, from the runtime trace:
```
matmul_int8_fast:fail_rate=0.135
matmul_int8_prefetch:fail_rate=0.02
attention_int8_kv:fail_rate=0.09
attention_bf16_path:invocations+=412
```
sophie: The pattern: after ~600-900 tokens we start to see more evictions, then a short burst where the int8 kernel misses and we fallback to bf16 kernels, runtime increases ~18% p95 latency, and memory doesn't shrink due to slot fragmentation — pages get partially reused but not coalesced.
maria: Could be two things: (1) quantized KV page layout + slot fragmentation prevents tight packing, (2) eviction thresholds tuned for steady short sessions, not long tails. Try increasing the cold-to-hot residency threshold and enable the `kv_compact_on_eviction=true` experiment.
kevin: Also try toggling `kernel_retry_mode=aggressive_prefetch` on the worker. It trades some CPU for fewer int8 misses (we saw that patch reduce matmul_int8_fast fail_rate to ~0.03 in perf runs).
jonathan: Warning: aggressive prefetch + compaction may affect accuracy because we might change reuse order for per-token caches. Did you run evals on the promptset with the changed heuristics?
sophie: ran a quick eval on our conversational QA set: next-token match went from 93.2% (bf16 baseline) -> 92.6% (int8 default profiles with current eviction) -> 92.9% (int8 + aggressive_prefetch + compact_on_eviction). So the heuristics recovered some of the perf/accuracy loss.
jonathan: Good. Can you attach the small regression harness (sample config + seed) so we can A/B with Optimize? If it consistently improves both mem footprint and accuracy, we can roll to canary.
sophie: config snippet I used:
```
{ "kv": { "quant_profile": "int8-default-v3", "eviction_threshold": 0.28, "compact_on_eviction": true, "prefetch_window": 48 }, "runtime": { "kernel_retry_mode": "aggressive_prefetch", "batching": { "max_tokens": 1024 } }
```
sophie: One more oddity: compact_on_eviction helps reclaim internal slot holes for >75% of the cases, but in ~10% we observe a small regress (memory spikes) just before compaction, likely due to concurrent page migration; attaching the short trace id for perf: perf/2765556789/kv-inventory-compacttrace
perf-bot: Trace uploaded — perf/2765556789/kv-inventory-compacttrace (size 12MB). Quick summary: concurrent-page-move stalls observed at worker-3, avg stall 32ms, correlated with eviction bursts.
kevin: ok, next steps: (1) run a longer 10k-session stress with `compact_on_eviction` + `aggressive_prefetch` to confirm no long-term degrowth, (2) gather full kernel trace, (3) collect model-output diffs against bf16 baseline and push to `optimize` for automated scoring.
maria: also add a small metric to console: `kv_fragmentation_ratio` and `kv_compact_latency` so SREs can alert on compaction spikes.
sophie: will run the long stress tonight and post results tomorrow morning. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
